tools.name: list_tags
tools.doc: Returns the User's Tags. Always call before creating a new Tag.

tools.name: create_tag
tools.doc: Creates a Tag. Color must match /^#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}$/.

tools.name: update_tag
tools.doc: Renames or recolors an existing Tag. Pass only the fields to change. Color must match /^#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}$/.

tools.name: delete_tag
tools.doc: Deletes a Tag. Cascade-removes every task_tags row referencing it; affected Tasks remain. Use with care — if the Tag was a Primary Tag, those Tasks lose their dashboard color until retagged.

tools.name: list_tasks
tools.doc: Returns Tasks with embedded ordered Tag list. Position 0 = Primary Tag. status filters: 'active' (dashboard), 'deferred' (Later tab), 'completed' (Archive). Omit for all. Returns BOTH standalone Tasks and Child Tasks mixed together — each row carries its own `parent_task_id` (null for standalone, parent UUID for Child Tasks). If you want the User's actual Dashboard view (top-level only, no Children), use `list_top_level_tasks` instead. If you want one Family's Children, use `list_children`.

tools.name: list_top_level_tasks
tools.doc: Returns ONLY rows with `parent_task_id IS NULL` — strictly top-level. Use this when reasoning about 'what's on the User's plate right now' — feeding raw list_tasks output as the Dashboard would double-render Child Tasks. status filters as in list_tasks. Note: the iOS Dashboard ALSO surfaces orphan Children (Children whose Parent is currently in Later or Archive) at the top level until the Parent is restored, so this query returns a *subset* of what the User sees the moment a Parent is deferred. To exactly mirror the Dashboard, combine this with a second pass that fetches Children whose Parent is not active (via list_children for each non-active Parent UUID you find through list_tasks status=deferred|completed). Most agents can ignore this nuance — list_top_level_tasks is fine for 'what's on the User's plate right now'; the orphan-children rule only matters for sub-second-accurate Dashboard mirroring.

tools.name: list_children
tools.doc: Returns one Family's Children — the Tasks whose `parent_task_id` matches the given UUID. Pass the Parent's UUID as parent_task_id. Optionally pass status to filter to active / completed / deferred Children. Rows are ordered by base_score desc — agents reasoning about urgency should still compute Effective Score client-side from base_score, due_date, and now (same as the Dashboard). To get all of a Parent's history (active + completed Children for a Family summary), call without a status filter.

tools.name: create_task
tools.doc: Creates a Task with the agent's chosen Base Score. Pass parent_task_id to create a Child Task directly under an existing Parent (Family); omit or pass null for a standalone Task. If you already know the Tag list at creation time, prefer create_task_with_tags — it is atomic and avoids the window where the Task has no Primary Tag. Server-side guards (migration 0019): parent_task_id must reference a row you own and that row must itself be top-level (no grandchildren — depth is capped at one). Attaching a Child to a completed Parent is rejected with 22023.

tools.name: create_task_with_tags
tools.doc: Atomic Task creation with an ordered Tag list. First UUID in p_tag_ids becomes the Primary Tag (position 0). Preferred over create_task + set_task_tags when the Tag list is known up-front — single transaction, no in-between window where the Task has no Primary Tag. Pass p_parent_task_id to create a Child Task under an existing Parent (Family). When the User says something like 'break this Task down into pieces' or 'add three subtasks under X', call this in a loop with p_parent_task_id = X. Child Tasks do NOT inherit the Parent's Tags automatically — pass p_tag_ids explicitly if the Children should be tagged.

tools.name: update_task
tools.doc: Patch any subset of mutable fields on a Task. parent_task_id is patchable here too — passing null promotes a Child Task to standalone; passing a UUID moves it under a new Parent — but prefer set_task_parent for the named-verb semantics and so the operation is legible in agent transcripts.

tools.name: complete_task
tools.doc: Sets status to completed. completed_at is set by a server trigger. The Task moves to the Archive. **Family rule (enforced server-side, migration 0019):** A Parent Task cannot be completed while any of its Children are non-completed — the server returns 22023 with 'cannot complete a family while it has active children'. Complete the Children first, then the Parent. Completing a Child is always allowed and never auto-completes the Parent.

tools.name: defer_task
tools.doc: Sets status to deferred. deferred_at is set by a server trigger. The Task leaves the dashboard and appears on the Later tab. Base Score is preserved — restore_task brings it back to the dashboard at its original position. Deferring a Child Task is allowed (it leaves the Family's active list but stays attached as a Child); deferring a Parent moves only the Parent — Children remain on the Dashboard.

tools.name: restore_task
tools.doc: Sets status to active. Restores a Task from Later (deferred) or from the Archive (completed) back onto the dashboard. deferred_at and completed_at are cleared by server triggers.

tools.name: set_task_tags
tools.doc: Replace the ordered Tag list on a Task. First ID becomes Primary. Empty array clears the list.

tools.name: set_task_parent
tools.doc: Move a Task between Families or make it standalone. Pass p_parent_task_id = <parent-uuid> to nest the Task under that Parent; pass null to promote the Task to standalone (it returns to the top-level Dashboard). Server-side guards (migration 0019): the Parent must be a row owned by the caller, must itself be top-level (no grandchildren — depth is capped at one), must not be completed, and the Task being moved must not itself have Children (no promote-with-children — that would create grandchildren via the back door). Returns the updated Task. Errors: 42501 if the Task isn't yours; 23503 if the Parent isn't yours or doesn't exist (same error — the server does not distinguish, to close the cross-tenant UUID-existence oracle); 22023 for depth / self-parent / completed-parent / promote-with-children violations.

tools.name: list_checklist_items
tools.doc: Returns Checklist Items for a Task, ordered by position ascending. Checklist Items are flat boolean steps under one Task — distinct from Child Tasks (which are full Tasks nested under a Parent). Use Checklist Items for 'the literal steps I will perform' (call, email, file); use Child Tasks (create_task_with_tags with p_parent_task_id) for 'an independent unit of work that deserves its own score, tags, and due date.'

tools.name: add_checklist_item
tools.doc: Append a Checklist Item to a Task. position is a double-precision rank — to insert between two siblings, use (above_position + below_position) / 2. For append, use (max_position + 1).

tools.name: update_checklist_item
tools.doc: Patch a Checklist Item: rename (text), toggle (is_done), or reorder (position). Pass only the fields you want to change. completed_at is maintained client-side; the server does not own it.

tools.name: delete_checklist_item
tools.doc: Delete a Checklist Item.

tools.name: list_comments
tools.doc: Returns Comments on a Task, oldest first, with any Comment-attached Attachments embedded. Use this to read the progress log on a Task.

tools.name: add_comment
tools.doc: Append a Comment to a Task. Use Comments to log progress ("called the contractor — no answer") instead of mutating the Task's notes field.

tools.name: update_comment
tools.doc: Edit a Comment's body. The server enforces a 5-minute edit window from created_at — older Comments will 403. If you need to add a follow-up after the window, post a new Comment.

tools.name: delete_comment
tools.doc: Delete a Comment. Allowed at any age — only edits have a 5-minute window. Cascade-removes any Attachments belonging to this Comment.

tools.name: list_attachments
tools.doc: Returns Attachment metadata (id, kind, remote_path, byte_size, created_at) for a Task. Returns only directly-task-attached rows; Comment-attached Attachments are reached via list_comments (embedded). The metadata does not include the blob — use get_attachment_url to fetch the actual file.

tools.name: get_attachment_url
tools.doc: Returns a short-lived (60s) signed URL for an Attachment's blob in Storage as { url: string, expires_in: int }. The agent can GET that URL once to fetch the file bytes. Don't cache — request a fresh one when you need to read. Implemented as a virtual RPC in the api-key-auth Edge Function (not a Postgres function): the function does an RLS-gated ownership check first, then signs server-side.

tools.name: request_attachment_upload
tools.doc: Step 1 of 3 for attaching a file to a Task. Validates ownership, size cap (25 MiB), MIME allowlist, and daily caps (5 uploads / 50 MiB per 24h). Returns { attachment_id, upload_url, expires_at }. Use the URL with PUT within 60 seconds. Daily caps charge on request — don't request unless you intend to upload.

tools.name: confirm_attachment_upload
tools.doc: Step 3 of 3. Flips a pending_upload row to synced once the PUT has landed. Returns false if the blob is not yet visible in Storage (retry) or if the row was already confirmed. The iPhone hides pending_upload rows; the row becomes user-visible only after this call succeeds.

tools.name: get_storage_stats
tools.doc: Returns { attachment_count, bytes_used, uploads_today_count, bytes_today, daily_upload_limit, daily_bytes_limit }. Useful before request_attachment_upload to check whether you'd hit the daily cap.
